reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 describes twinning-induced plasticity in a different fcc medium-entropy alloy (CrCoNi) at cryogenic/room temperature, not in refractory bcc HEAs at high temperature. E2 lists prior mechanical properties of some refractory HEAs but provides no data on WTaTiVZr or its deformation mechanisms. E3 mentions creep testing of TaTiVWZr but does not report twin or dislocation network formation. Thus, the specific mechanistic claims about lattice distortion causing nano-twins and dislocation networks in WTaTiVZr are unsupported by the cite
premises: Lattice distortion in equimolar WTaTiVZr promotes nanoscale deformation twins at high temperature.
Lattice distortion promotes a complex dislocation network at high temperature.
Nanoscale twins and dislocation networks together impede crack propagation and facilitate plastic strain.
This combined mechanism yields significantly enhanced toughness and ductility compared to pure tungsten.
